Title: Who is this for, in one sentence?
Detail_lesson: Name a real kind of person and the moment they would use it. "Busy volunteers on a Saturday morning" helps Claude more than "everyone".
CustomInstruction: One sentence: a person and a moment.
Placeholder: One sentence: a person and a moment.
ClaudeNote: Treat the winning answer as the audience for every screen and every word on it.

Title: Who is this not for?
Detail_lesson: Saying who it is not for is how a small thing stays small and good.
CustomInstruction: Name a kind of person, not a feature.
Placeholder: Name a kind of person, not a feature.
ClaudeNote: Do not build for these people. If a later direction would serve them, say so first.

Title: Who did we forget?
Detail_lesson: Someone who cannot read small text, someone new to the language, someone who has never used an app like this, someone in a hurry.
CustomInstruction: Name one person and what gets in their way.
Placeholder: Name one person and what gets in their way.
ClaudeNote: Check the build works for the winning answer, say what fails for them, and keep them in mind from now on.

Title: What job is someone hiring this to do?
Detail_lesson: People do not want a sign-up form. They want to know where to be on Saturday. What are they really trying to get done?
ClaudeNote: Use the winning job as the test for every feature: does it help with this job?

Title: What does done look like by the end of today?
Detail_lesson: Not everything it could become. What could someone do with it when this session ends?
ClaudeNote: Use this as the finish line. When it is true, say so and suggest wrapping up.

Title: What must it never do?
Detail_lesson: Lose someone's details? Ask for a password? Take more than a minute? Name the line it must not cross.
ClaudeNote: Treat the winning answers as hard rules. If a later direction would break one, say so before you build.

Title: It is launch day. Write the headline.
Detail_lesson: Some teams start a product by writing the news story first, then build what the story promises. Write the headline a local paper would run on the day this goes live.
ClaudeNote: Read the winning headline as the promise the product has to keep, and build toward it.

Title: What should the first version do?
Detail_lesson: One thing done well beats three half done.
Options: Show something|Let people do one thing|Do the whole job, roughly
ClaudeNote: Build the first version to the winning level, and say what you left out.

Title: Should it work on a phone first?
Detail_lesson: Think of where people will open it.
ClaudeNote: If most say yes, design for a phone screen first and widen later. If no, design for a laptop.

Title: How could we reach the same goal a completely different way?
Detail_lesson: Forget what is on the screen. If we started again with the same goal, what would we build instead?
CustomInstruction: Describe the other way in one or two sentences.
Placeholder: Describe the other way in one or two sentences.
ClaudeNote: In a few lines, say how you would build the winning approach and what it would cost next to the current one. Do not switch unless a Do now says so.

Title: How would we do this with no app at all?
Detail_lesson: A paper sheet on a door, a text message, a phone call round. What would work, and what would we lose?
CustomInstruction: Name the low-tech way and what it does well.
Placeholder: Name the low-tech way and what it does well.
ClaudeNote: Say which part of the winning answer the build could borrow, if any, and what it would replace.

Title: Who has solved this already, in a different field?
Detail_lesson: A restaurant booking, a doctor's appointment, a parcel on its way. What do they do that we could borrow?
CustomInstruction: Name the example and the one thing worth borrowing.
Placeholder: Name the example and the one thing worth borrowing.
ClaudeNote: Say what you would borrow from the winning example and where it would go on the screen.

Title: How would we make sure nobody ever used it?
Detail_lesson: Turn the problem around: list the surest ways to make it fail. Then we avoid them.
CustomInstruction: One sure way to fail per answer.
Placeholder: One sure way to fail per answer.
ClaudeNote: Turn each winning answer into a rule in the brief: the opposite of how to fail.

Title: What would make this ten times better, not ten percent?
Detail_lesson: Small improvements come from polishing. Ten times better usually means doing it a different way.
CustomInstruction: Be bold; say what would have to be true.
Placeholder: Be bold; say what would have to be true.
ClaudeNote: Put the winning idea on the Later list, and say what the first small step toward it would be.

Title: What would stop someone using it?
Detail_lesson: Think of the busiest person you know, on an old phone, in a hurry. Where do they give up?
CustomInstruction: Name the moment they give up, not a feature you want.
Placeholder: Name the moment they give up, not a feature you want.
ClaudeNote: Fix the top answer first. Say in one line what you changed.

Title: What is confusing on the screen right now?
Detail_lesson: Look at what is on the wall. What did you have to read twice?
CustomInstruction: Point at one thing on the screen.
Placeholder: Point at one thing on the screen.
ClaudeNote: Treat each answer as a specific problem. Fix the top one and show it before and after.

Title: What should we cut?
Detail_lesson: A thing is finished not when nothing more can be added, but when nothing more can be taken away. What on the screen could go?
ClaudeNote: Remove the winning item unless it breaks a Keep in mind rule. Say what you removed.

Title: What matters most next?
Detail_lesson: Pick one; the others wait.
Options: How it looks|What it does|How easy it is to start
ClaudeNote: Spend the next step on the winning choice. Say what you changed.

Title: Is it clear what to do first?
Detail_lesson: Look at the first screen as someone new.
ClaudeNote: If most say no, make the first step the most obvious thing on the screen.

Title: How close is this to something you would use?
Detail_lesson: Think of the moment you would actually need it.
ClaudeNote: Use the average and the reasons to decide whether to keep polishing or move on. Say which.

Title: How clear is the main screen?
Detail_lesson: Could someone new use it without asking anyone?
ClaudeNote: If the average is under 4, fix the reason given most often before adding anything.

Title: A month from now, nobody uses it. Why?
Detail_lesson: Imagine it launched and failed. People find risks faster when they explain a failure that has already happened than when they guess at one that might.
CustomInstruction: Give the reason, as if it had happened.
Placeholder: Give the reason, as if it had happened.
ClaudeNote: Add the top reasons to the Later list as risks. Say which ones today's build already causes.

Title: What should we build next time?
Detail_lesson: The one thing you would want on the screen at the start of the next session.
ClaudeNote: Put the winning answers on the Later list for the next session.

Title: Is it ready to show someone outside this room?
Detail_lesson: Ready means they could use it without us explaining.
ClaudeNote: If most say no, fix what they name before wrapping up.

Title: Would you use this tomorrow?
Detail_lesson: Honestly, for real, tomorrow.
ClaudeNote: Put this score and its top reason in the wrap-up summary.
